# Answer

**The duck third from the left looks uncomfortable.**

## Which moment this is

The cartoon is the 1930 Looney Tunes short *"The Booze Hangs High."* The first ducks in the
film appear when the picture cuts to a barnyard path at **≈2:06 (126.1 s)**: a big mother duck
in a flower-trimmed straw hat waddling along with **three ducklings walking single file in a
row** ahead of her, the camera panning right to follow them.

They walk continuously for about ten seconds. I measured the pan frame by frame (horizontal
background shift at 12 fps) and it is constant from 126.1 s until it drops to exactly zero at
**≈2:16 (136.1 s)** — that is the first time the three ducks in a row come to a stop. They then
hold still in that row for roughly two seconds, until about 138.0 s, when the third duckling
opens its bill and the group starts its quacking/singing number.

Counting left to right in that stopped row, the ducklings are #1, #2, #3, with the mother duck
standing to the right of all three. So "third from the left" is the rightmost duckling, the one
standing closest to the mother.

## What the third duckling looks like during the stop

Its two siblings and it are drawn very differently once they halt:

- **Ducklings #1 and #2** turn their heads into profile facing left, with their bills curved up
  into clear little smiles, eyes glancing off to the side, and both wings held out loosely away
  from their bodies. They read as happy and relaxed.
- **Duckling #3** does not turn. It stays square-on to the camera, staring straight out at the
  viewer with two big, wide-open oval eyes that never blink or shift. Its bill is shut flat with
  the corners turned down — there is no smile at all. Its head is pulled down into its shoulders
  so no neck shows, and its wings hang limp and pinned flat against its sides rather than held
  out like its siblings'. The dark fringe of feather tufts over its brow reads as a knitted,
  furrowed forehead. It holds this pose completely frozen for the whole ~2-second stop, and when
  it finally does move (≈138.0 s) the bill first opens into a downturned grimace before it turns
  its head and quacks.

## Why "uncomfortable" rather than the other options

- **Not happy.** There is no smile; the bill is clamped shut and the corners droop. The contrast
  with the two grinning siblings right next to it is the whole point of the staging.
- **Not excited.** Excitement would show as bouncing, spread wings, or an open bill. This duckling
  is rigid and motionless, with its wings clamped down — the least energetic figure on screen.
- **Not surprised.** The eyes are wide, which is the one thing that points that way, but nothing
